analysis.title: DB CoTD - World Outlook 2027: Great Expectations, but Risky Business
key_insights: DB publishes its 2027 World Outlook titled 'Great Expectations, but Risky Business', framed after last week's savage equity sell-off.
DB equity strategists see the recent sell-off as a significant vol event that does not derail fundamentals, and target S&P 500 at 9,000 by year-end 2027 on extremely supportive earnings.
AI is expected to have a significant productivity impact. AI-related capex is already large enough to influence US growth and early signs show stronger productivity in AI-intensive sectors.
History warns that capex-led technological revolutions rarely go smoothly. Overinvestment, busts and unexpected winners and losers are part of the path.
Geopolitics could drive the largest forecast errors. Russia-Ukraine ceasefire pressure may rise, US-China tech competition likely intensifies, and the Middle East remains an energy risk.
Brent is forecast to fall from around $90/bbl in Q1 to about $70 in H2 2027, though the call is highly geopolitically contingent.

Rates strategists are broadly neutral on duration after being bearish in recent years and expect steeper curves. Supply, fiscal demands and supply shocks keep equilibrium rates and term premia above 2010s norms.
FX strategists expect a higher-for-longer dollar, with EUR/USD falling to 1.08 in H1 2027 before recovering to 1.15 by end-2027.
DB forecasts the Fed funds rate rising to 4.63 by Q1-27 and holding through Q4-27, then easing to 3.88 by Q3-28.
DB forecasts the 10Y UST at about 5.0% through 2027 and 5.1% by Q4-27, with the current level at 5.0.
DB global growth forecast: World GDP 3.5% in 2026 (per table), US 2.3%, China 4.6/4.5/4.3 path, India 7.2% 2027.
Credit spreads are forecast to widen modestly: US HY from 344 currently to 375 by Q4-27, US IG from 92 to 100.

sector_views.rationale: AI productivity and capex support earnings and the 9,000 S&P target, but overinvestment risk is flagged.

earnings_insights: DB equity strategists describe earnings as extremely supportive for the S&P 500 reaching 9,000 by year-end 2027 (forecast, no EPS figure given).

macro_indicators.interpretation: DB expects hikes from 3.88 in Q3-26 to a 4.63 plateau, then cuts in 2028.
Structurally higher term premia keep long yields elevated.

macro_indicators.reading: $90 in Q1-27F falling to $70 in H2-27F
macro_indicators.interpretation: Oil provides baseline relief but is geopolitically contingent.
Dollar stays strong near term before recovering.
Implies about 25% upside from the 7,176 current level.
Steady US growth supported by AI capex.

risk_factors: AI capex overinvestment and bust risk.
S&P 9,000 target heavily exposed to the earnings and AI cycle.
Fiscal activism adds to bond supply and debt.
Rising government supply and term premia.
vol_and_positioning: Last week's savage equity sell-off is viewed by DB equity strategists as a significant vol event but not a fundamental derailment.
DB expects 2027 to be another volatile year even if the overall outcome is good.
geopolitical: Pressure for a Russia-Ukraine ceasefire may increase but European security challenges persist.
US-China competition likely to intensify across strategic technologies.
Middle East remains an important source of energy risk.
Strategic autonomy requires huge defence, energy and technology spending and adds to geopolitical tensions.

Brent forecast to fall from around $90/bbl
EUR/USD falling to 1.08 in H1 before recovering to 1.15 by end-2027

tension_points.bear_case: Capex-led technological revolutions rarely go smoothly and overinvestment and busts are part of the journey.
